subject.title: fix(agents): avoid synthetic overflow in tool-heavy sessions

question: Should OpenClaw adopt provider rejection, rather than local aggregate/preflight/tool-loop character estimates, as the authority for whole-session compaction recovery in embedded-agent runs?
rationale: The patch is internally coherent and proven, but this is an intentional compatibility policy change in session recovery that can preserve more history while shifting when recovery occurs; repository policy requires owner confirmation for behavior and compatibility-sensitive changes.

options.title: Approve provider-authoritative recovery
options.body: Accept the broader policy after merge-head CI completes, preserving local estimates for prompt shaping and diagnostics but reserving whole-session recovery for provider-confirmed overflow.

options.title: Keep conservative local recovery
options.body: Reject the policy change and retain synthetic local admission, accepting the reported premature-compaction behavior until a different recovery contract is designed.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Adopt only the linked aggregate-projection mitigation and leave preflight and tool-loop policy unchanged, with the remaining false-positive paths tracked separately.

recommendation.title: Approve provider-authoritative recovery
recommendation.body: Accept the broader policy after merge-head CI completes, preserving local estimates for prompt shaping and diagnostics but reserving whole-session recovery for provider-confirmed overflow.

likelyOwner.reason: Most concrete implementation and proof history available in this review is concentrated in the current patch series; an agent-runtime owner should make the final policy call.
